electric.contrast: Hot centre of the primary glow; royal so that white type keeps 5.4:1 measured beside it

electric-soft.contrast: Hot centre of the secondary glow at 70%

sky.contrast: 11.30:1 on night; 7:1 or better where used; about 3.5:1 at a glow peak

panel.contrast: 1.06:1 over ground; separated by the seam

seam.contrast: 1.34:1 on ground; structural, never sole meaning

white.contrast: Résumé label (4.63:1 on Signal Blue) and the hero strip bars

lift.contrast: Raised tile behind each More work mark

night.contrast: Base of the grainy surface; white on it 20.38:1

glass.contrast: Laid on the blue at 55-60% opacity; white on it over a glow 13.8:1 or better

on-blue.contrast: 20.38:1 on night; 6.1-6.4:1 at the brightest glow point

on-blue-soft.contrast: Resolves to white: tints measured 4.0-4.3:1 beside the brightest glow with grain

on-blue-label.contrast: Resolves to white: hierarchy on the blue comes from size, weight and mono labels

display.purpose: The name on the wide hero only; On-Blue White, speckled.

headline.purpose: Project names in card header bands; speckled; shrinks by 1px to fit, never truncated.

stat.purpose: The four activity numbers (21px narrow); speckled.

lede.purpose: The hero pitch in On-Blue Soft.

lede-narrow.purpose: The hero pitch on the 360px hero.

tagline.purpose: The project tagline in each header band, On-Blue Soft.

body.purpose: Card descriptions in Soft Steel; More work descriptions at 14.5px.

row-title.purpose: Project names on More work rows, Console White.

chip.purpose: Technology names inside chips, Console White.

value.purpose: Card fact values and feed sentences; hero values at 13.5px (13px narrow).

command.purpose: The now-shipping line; 'docsforge' at 500 in Sky (11.5px narrow).

data.purpose: Title-bar paths and statuses, hero keys, strip total; card paths and feed dates at 12px.

flow.purpose: Step names inside flow nodes, On-Blue White (11px narrow).

data-small.purpose: Chart axis (10.5px), busiest-week note, status bar (11.5px wide).

tag.purpose: Status pill labels, sentence case, On-Blue White (11px narrow).

label.purpose: Uppercase labels inside panels and Tech stack group names (10.5px narrow).

key.purpose: Uppercase field keys above values (10px narrow).

motion.name: breath
motion.purpose: The page's only animation: the halo around the hero's Sky availability dot (Canvas.pulse).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Shipped in every SVG by Canvas.svg(); the dot then rests with a static 18% halo.

canvases.name: wide
canvases.note: viewBox width of every wide panel

textures.name: console-grain
textures.value: feTurbulence fractalNoise baseFrequency .9, numOctaves 2, seed 7, desaturated, alpha 0..0.14
textures.purpose: Fine grain on every console panel ground (Canvas.panel).

textures.name: dot-grid
textures.purpose: Faint lattice on console panels only; never on the blue surface.

textures.name: glow-primary
textures.value: radialGradient #1D4ED8 .95 -> #1F6FEB .55 at 45% -> 0; centre outside the box
textures.purpose: The light entering each grainy surface from an edge. Hero wide (16%,118%) r .85w; narrow (10%,105%) r 1.1w; cards per-card point, r .7w.

textures.name: glow-secondary
textures.purpose: Fainter light in the opposite corner. Hero wide (96%,-25%) r .55w; cards (1-gx, -60%) r .45w.

textures.name: white-specks
textures.value: feTurbulence fractalNoise .78, 3 octaves, seed s; white, alpha 3.2n - 1.68; layer opacity .42
textures.purpose: Visible white film grain on the blue surface.

textures.name: black-specks
textures.value: feTurbulence fractalNoise .78, 3 octaves, seed s+31; black, alpha 1.5 - 3.2n; layer opacity .5
textures.purpose: Black film grain on the blue surface. Seeds: hero 4; cards 7 + len(key).

textures.name: glass
textures.value: #050811 at 55% (command box, flow nodes) or 60% (pills); white hairline 16-22%; no blur
textures.purpose: Boxes laid on the blue surface.

textures.name: hairline-on-blue
textures.purpose: Separation on the blue, in place of Seam Steel.

textures.name: speckle
textures.value: feTurbulence fractalNoise baseFrequency .95, numOctaves 2, seed 11, tone .5..1.25, multiplied into the mark
textures.purpose: Grain inside large lit marks: hero name, project names, stat numbers, all chart and strip bars, Résumé fill.

narrative.overview:
The profile is a formal developer console, not a themed costume: a dashboard of shipped systems in blue and black. Every visual is an SVG drawn by Python (`scripts/console.py` is the shared kit), because GitHub strips CSS and JS from READMEs. The system has two grounds and uses each for one job. The **grainy blue surface** (`Canvas.grainy()`) carries identity: the hero card and the header band of every project card, where a near-black Night is lit by two soft electric-blue glows entering from an edge, under visible white and black film grain, with type in three whites. The **console panel** (`Canvas.panel()`) carries detail: GitHub's own dark ground, a 1px seam around a 12px frame, a faint dot grid and fine grain, used for card bodies, the More work rows, the Tech stack and the Activity panel. Content is set in two faces, Geist for words and Geist Mono for data. Blue is the only hue, and one dot on the whole page breathes.

The register is "somewhat formal" (PRODUCT.md, confirmed by the user). Density is dashboard-like but calm: short labels, key/value rows, chips, numbers set large, sentences kept to one or two lines. Personality lives in a few precise details: the grain in the blue and in the lit marks (the name, the project names, the numbers, the bars, the Résumé fill), the live 26-week strip of white bars and the 52-week chart redrawn twice a day by a GitHub Action, the "how it works" flow drawn across each project header, monochrome technology marks, and the hidden flag for security people. Two earlier worlds were rejected outright, stacked medical imaging and a demoscene cracktro title screen; nothing from either survives.

Everything stays opaque in both GitHub themes on purpose. In dark mode the console panels sit flush with the page and the blue surfaces glow out of it; in light mode every panel reads as an embedded console screen. Nothing in the README swaps by theme: section headings are GitHub's own markdown `##` headings.
keyCharacteristics: Two opaque grounds with fixed jobs: the grainy blue surface for identity (hero, project headers), the console panel for detail (card bodies, rows, stack, activity).
Geist for words, Geist Mono for data; uppercase only on small tracked mono field labels.
Blue is the only hue; each tone has one job, and Sky is the only blue that sits on the blue.
One blue button (Résumé); the blue surface is a ground for identity, never an action.
Exactly one animation: the hero's availability dot breathing; still under reduced motion.
Every panel exists twice: 830px wide and a recomposed 360px narrow drawing; buttons are natural size.
Live panels (hero, activity) are redrawn twice a day; all other panels are static builds.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Blue is the only hue on the page. Signal Blue fills, Live Blue marks state on the console, Readout Blue is blue text and technology marks on the console, Sky is blue on the blue. No green for "online", no red, no amber, and no brand colours on technology marks; state is said in blue tones and words.

rules.name: The Two Palettes Rule
rules.body: Type on the grainy surface is only white (the three on-blue roles all resolve to #FFFFFF; hierarchy there comes from size, weight and mono labels), and Sky is only for marks, arrows and text inside a Glass box; type on the console ground uses only Console White, Soft Steel, Key Grey and the console blues. Never carry a colour across: Live Blue or Readout Blue vanish into the glow, and On-Blue Label is not a console grey.

rules.name: The One Blue Button Rule
rules.body: The Résumé button is the only button filled blue. Every other action is a Raised Slate box with a seam. The grainy blue surface is a ground for identity, never an action.

rules.name: The Opaque Console Rule
rules.body: Every panel is opaque (Console Black or Night) in both GitHub themes. Nothing is drawn twice for light and dark; headings are markdown, so GitHub themes them.

rules.name: The Words and Data Rule
rules.body: Geist sets what a person reads as language (names, sentences, values, chip and button labels). Geist Mono sets what a machine would print (paths, keys, dates, counts in captions, commands, pipeline steps, labels). Never swap them for effect.

rules.name: The Field Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase appears only in Geist Mono 500 at 10 to 11px with positive tracking, and only to name a field or a group. A label never sits above a larger headline as a kicker. A title-bar path is a location, lowercase, and always shares its row with a status.

rules.name: The Measured Text Rule
rules.body: Every string is placed with `measure()`, `wrap()` or `fit()` from `console.py`, which use advance widths from `scripts/fonts/metrics.json` without kerning; leave a few pixels of slack. A character outside the committed set (`BASIC` in `build_assets.py`: ASCII plus `·×→↗•★–—…’é®`) has no metrics and no glyph in the live subsets until it is added there and the build is rerun.

rules.name: The Two Drawings Rule
rules.body: Every panel that would otherwise scale gets a 360px `-narrow` drawing, recomposed for the phone column (stacked facts, wrapped flows, chips under labels, 2 x 2 stats), and served by `<source media="(max-width: 600px)">`. Never rely on GitHub shrinking an 830px drawing.

rules.name: The One-Line Picture Rule
rules.body: A `<picture>` block stays on a single line. Multi-line picture blocks inside a link break on GitHub.

rules.name: The Seam and Glass Rule
rules.body: On the console ground, separation is a 1px seam and one tonal step. On the blue, it is a white hairline and a Glass box. No drop shadows, no blur or backdrop filter anywhere, and glows exist only inside `grainy()`.

rules.name: The Grain in the Light Rule
rules.body: Grain lives on every ground (fine grey grain on the console, white and black specks on the blue); speckle lives only in large lit marks (display and headline type, stat numbers, bars, the one blue button). Never speckle text under about 21px, secondary copy, or icons.

rules.name: The One Breath Rule
rules.body: One thing moves on the whole page: the hero's availability dot. Every other status dot (now-shipping, status pills, activity "Live") is a static 3.5px circle. Never add a second animation.

rules.name: The Identity Band Rule
rules.body: A project card opens with a grainy header band that says what the thing is and how it works (path, status, name, tagline, flow) and closes with a console body that proves it (description, stack, facts). Facts never go on the blue.

dos: Do change colours, type and icons in `scripts/console.py` (and `SKY` in both `hero.py` and `build_assets.py`), then run both `build_assets.py` and `activity.py`; never hand-edit `assets/*.svg` (the Action overwrites the hero and activity twice a day).
Do draw identity on `Canvas.grainy()` and detail on `Canvas.panel()`, at 830px with a recomposed 360px `-narrow` twin served by `<source media="(max-width: 600px)">`, on one line inside its link.

Do keep each blue to its job: Signal Blue (#1F6FEB) fills and glow bodies, Live Blue (#58A6FF) state marks and icons on the console, Readout Blue (#79C0FF) blue text and technology marks on the console, Sky (#93C5FD) anything blue on the blue.
Do set type on the blue only in On-Blue White (content), On-Blue Soft (sentences) and On-Blue Label (small labels), and lay boxes on the blue as Glass with a white hairline.
Do set words in Geist and data in Geist Mono, and place every string with `measure()`, `wrap()` or `fit()`.
Do draw technology marks from Simple Icons in one colour, and fall back to a line icon when the mark is unreadable at 16px.
Do give every image an alt that is a complete text equivalent, and keep live numbers out of README alt text (only the SVGs are redrawn).
Do put links that matter in a button row under the card; an SVG cannot carry a working link.
Do add any new character to `BASIC` in `build_assets.py` and rerun it before a live panel uses it.
Do preview with `python3 scripts/activity.py --demo --out-dir <somewhere outside assets>`.
donts: Don't add a second hue: no green "online", red error or amber warning, and no brand colours on technology marks; state is blue and words.
Don't fill a second button blue or make the blue surface clickable-looking; Résumé is the one blue action.
Don't animate anything besides the hero's availability dot, and don't remove the reduced-motion rule from `Canvas.svg()`.
Don't add drop shadows, blur or backdrop filters, or glows outside `grainy()`.
Don't put console colours (Console White, Soft Steel, Key Grey, Live Blue, Readout Blue) on the blue surface, or on-blue whites on the console ground.
Don't make panels transparent or draw light-theme variants; nothing swaps by theme.
Don't speckle small text, secondary copy or icons.
Don't put a mono uppercase label above a larger headline as a kicker; labels name fields and groups.
Don't split a `<picture>` block across lines.
Don't truncate a project name; shrink it.
Don't put a small label at a glow's brightest point.
Don't bring back the rejected worlds (stacked medical imaging, the cracktro title screen) or any playful costume; the register is somewhat formal.
knownDefects: The faintest bars fall below 3:1 non-text contrast: in the activity chart, 45% Signal Blue (about 1.7:1 on the ground) and the Seam Steel zero-week stubs (1.34:1); in the hero strip, 45% white (about 2.6:1 against the glow behind it) and the 28% zero-week stubs (about 1.85:1). The totals, stats, desc and alt carry the data, so this is tolerated; it is not a value to reuse for a mark that carries meaning on its own.

Contrast of type on the blue was measured on rendered pixels: at the 95th percentile of the background beside the brightest-placed text (white grain specks included), L is about 0.146, where white holds 5.4:1. Any tint fell to 4.0 to 4.3:1 there, which is why every word on the blue is white. Re-measure if a glow moves closer to text or the grain gets stronger.

This build was checked with github.com's rendered HTML for the README and the local SVGs (Edge, 900px and a 390px phone frame, both themes). The GitHub mobile app was not checked; if it ignores `<source media>`, it falls back to the wide drawings scaled down.
